150.25.20.1(1).explanation: A building with a multi-tenant house may also contain dwelling units, up to the zone's maximum number of dwelling units. The total number of dwelling rooms (not counting bedrooms in a dwelling unit) must stay within the room limits in subsections (3) to (5).

150.25.20.1(2).explanation: A multi-tenant house needs at least one sanitary facility (toilet, wash basin, and bath or shower) for every four dwelling rooms, rounded up to a whole number.

150.25.20.1(3).explanation: In the R, RD, RS, RT and RM zones a multi-tenant house is allowed in a building originally built as one or in any building type allowed with dwelling units. It is limited to 6 dwelling rooms per lot, or 12 in an R zone inside a 12 Dwelling Room Special Area. These rules apply in RM zones whose label has a u value of 6 or less, or no u value. A multi-tenant house without a dwelling unit follows the requirements for a detached house, or for the matching portion of a semi-detached house or townhouse.

150.25.20.1(4).explanation: In the RA, RAC and RM zones a multi-tenant house is allowed in a building originally built as one or in any building type allowed with dwelling units. It is limited to 6 dwelling rooms per lot in a 6 Dwelling Room Special Area and 12 elsewhere. Without a dwelling unit it follows the requirements for a residential building.

150.25.20.1(5).explanation: In the CR and CRE zones a multi-tenant house is allowed in a building originally built as one or in any building type allowed with dwelling units. It is limited to 6 dwelling rooms per lot in a 6 Dwelling Room Special Area and 25 elsewhere. Without a dwelling unit it follows the requirements for a residential or mixed use building.
